sessions.title: Genealogy of the concept ‘environment’
sessions.description:
Steps towards developing a critical approach to the built environment

Revisiting dichotomies: e.g. primitive versus modern, colonial versus post-colonial, vernacular versus capital A architecture

sessions.title: Social Life of Things – The Ecological System’s Approach
sessions.description: Religion, monuments and colonial built forms – India, Sub-Saharan Africa, Egypt

sessions.title: Modernist “IDEAL” built environments
sessions.description: e.g. Walter Gropius’ Bauhaus, Garden Cities and development corridors: Chandigarh, New Delhi, New Settlements

sessions.title: Time-Space Compression and early Ideas of socio-technical systems
sessions.description: Starchitects and seductive landscapes of consumption, affective built environments and the vertical city

sessions.title: Self-built environments and engineering the future
sessions.description:
Self-built environments and engineering the future including informal built environment in contrast to micro-biopolitics and energy-efficient settlements e.g. BedZed

Neoliberal built environments: What is “real” about Real Estate?
